paragraphs.text: 防止dsh自作主张上传到github Prevent DSH from uploading to GitHub on its own initiative
# Git Repository Guard · dsh-git-guard
中文说明 →

Two switches at the right of the Session header that stop an agent from writing your
local git repos
itory or uploading it to a remote.
| Switch | Position | What it blocks |
| Local repository | left | Writes to the local repository: `git add`, `git commit`, `git reset`, `g

it merge`, `git tag` and friends |
| Remote repository | right | Anything that reaches a remote: `gi
t push`, `git pull`, `git clone`, `git remote`, `gh` and friends |

Both start on. The block happens **before** a command runs: the call is not executed,
and the agent
gets a clear refusal instead.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Reload the page and the two switches appear at the right of the Session header.

> By hand: add `@yokira404/dsh-git-guard` to `dsh.profile.bundles` in
> `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/p

ackage.json`, and list it under `dependencies` as
> `"^1.0.1"`.
## How the two switches interact
Two rules, both the **consequence of a click** — never a condition that has to hold:
| Click | Local | Remote |
| left (local) | toggles | turns **on** with the local switch when that lands on; left alone when it

lands off |
| right (remote) | turns **off** with the remote switch when that lands off; left alone
when it lands on | toggles |
- **Switching a guard on never releases the other one.** Asking for one protection must not dismantl

e the other.
- **Releasing the upload guard releases the local one with it** — the local writes are

exactly what an upload would carry.
- One deliberate opening: **with both off, the right switch arms
the upload guard alone**, leaving local writes open.
All four states are reachable:
| State | Local writes | Uploads |

| on · on (default) | blocked | blocked |
| off · on | allowed | blocked |
| on · off | blocked | al

lowed |
| off · off | allowed | allowed |
## What is blocked
**Left switch** — writes to the local repository:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**Right switch** — anything that reaches a remote:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

**Never blocked**: `git status`, `git log`, `git diff`, `git show`, `git branch`,
`git blame`, `git

init`, `git rev-parse`, `git check-ignore`, `git ls-files`,
`git worktree`, `git help`, `gh auth`, `

gh config`, `gh api /user`, and anything that is
not about git at all. `git init` is allowed on purp

ose: creating a repository neither
commits nor uploads anything.

Matching is **quote-aware**: `git commit -m "do not push this"` is a local commit, not
an upload, an

d `echo "git push" > notes.txt` is nothing. It is not fooled by prefixes
either — `sudo git push`, `

env FOO=1 git commit` and
`C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe push` are all recognised.
## What the agent sees when it is blocked
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Limits

- **It never changes your repository**: no `.git/hooks`, no `git config`, blocking only.
- **It also

catches text that merely names a command**: matching reads the whole of a
tool call's command-like

field (`command`, `script`, `code`, …), so writing a document
whose text contains `git push` can hav

e that write blocked. That is the deliberate
bias — one extra blocked write beats one upload that go

t through.
- **It cannot stop paths that avoid the shell**; it targets the real one, an agent
upload

ing a repository through a command.
- **No undo**: the block is up front, so there is no window in w

hich something was
already uploaded.
- **State is not persisted**: a DSH restart returns both switch

thing was
already uploaded.
- **State is not persisted**: a DSH restart returns both switches to on.
